_comment: Extra models the router may use, merged over the built-in Anthropic catalog. Prices are US dollars per million tokens. Adding a model here needs no code change; the provider still has to be registered on the router, and its credential present, or the model is simply not usable.

_example.notes: Set OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL to make this usable.

models.notes: A second vendor, so routing quality becomes comparable at all. No server-side tools: an agent needing web search must not be routed here. Needs NVIDIA_API_KEY and NVIDIA_MODEL.
Needs XAI_API_KEY and XAI_MODEL. Verify the id against x.ai before relying on it.
Reached over Google's OpenAI-compatibility endpoint. Needs GEMINI_API_KEY and GEMINI_MODEL.

_nvidia_note: NVIDIA NIM speaks Chat Completions, so it reuses the OpenAI provider with a different base URL. Set NVIDIA_API_KEY and NVIDIA_MODEL to make an entry below usable. Prices here are 0.0 deliberately: the build.nvidia.com free tier is not metered per token, so a made-up figure would put fiction in the cost ledger. A 0.0 price means 'this model reports no cost', which is a different claim from 'this model is free' and the one the data supports.
_vendor_note: Four vendors reachable over Chat Completions: OpenAI, NVIDIA, xAI and Gemini. Each needs its own <VENDOR>_API_KEY and <VENDOR>_MODEL, or the provider does not register and its models are simply not usable. None declares supports_server_tools: Chat Completions has no equivalent of Anthropic's server-side web search, and the router filters on that flag — a wrong value would send a research agent to a model that cannot search and then blame the agent for citing nothing. Prices are 0.0 where the tier is not metered per token; 0.0 means 'reports no cost', which is a different claim from 'is free' and the only one the data supports.
